newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Prudential Singapore's life premiums surge.
newsitem.headline: Prudential Singapore's life premiums surge.

text.p: Prudential Corporation plc's Singapore unit said on Thursday its life insurance premiums surged to Singapore $272.5 million in 1996 and its outlook for 1997 was buoyed by a reform of Singapore's state pension scheme.
"I think we will be aided by the reform of the CPFIS (Central Provident Fund Investment Scheme). We expect a buoyant 1997," chief executive Tan Suee Chieh told Reuters.
Life insurance premiums in 1995 amounted to S$189.6 million.

Single premium business year on year in 1996 leapt 53.5 percent to S$177.9 million from S$115.9 million in 1995 and annual premium policies jumped 28.4 percent to S$94.6 million from S$73.7 million, the company said in a statement.
The growth gives Prudential a 25.9 percent share of single premium and a 15.1 percent share of annual premium life business in Singapore, the company said.
Growth was achieved against fierce competition from companies with more extensive distribution networks, Tan said.
But he said there were no plans for Prudential to change its traditional reliance on its agency network to combat this growing competition.
"There will be no significant shift away from our agency force," he said.
